predecessors.name: Scythian kingdom
predecessors.text: the Pontic steppe, as scythia's own successor entry gives it: 'By 200 BC, the Sarmatians replaced the Scythians as the dominant people of the steppes'; the first ground, beyond the Don, goes in 313 BC

successors.name: Gothia
successors.text: the western steppe where the Goths 'broke the Sarmatian dominance of the Pontic Steppe' in the 3rd century

successors.name: Huns
successors.text: the Alans east of the Don, whom the Huns conquered in 375

ledger.x: 313 BC: the Sarmatians cross the Don.
313 BC: the steppe beyond the Don passes from Scythia.
313 BC: the Sarmatian invasion of the Pontic steppe begins.
224 BC: the Sarmatians replace the Scythians on the Pontic steppe.

c. 100 BC: the Sarmatians reach the Danube. 'At their greatest reported extent, around 100 BC, these tribes could be found from the Danube and eastward to the Volga'; the Roxolani 'moved into the area between the Dnipro and the Danube' in the 1st century BC.

c. 44 BC: the Iazyges reach the Danube-Tisza steppe. 'In c. 44 BC, they moved into modern-day Hungary and Serbia near the Pannonian steppe between the Danube and Tisza rivers'; the same page also says c. 20 AD, 'taking absolute control of the territory from the Dacians', and Fitz c. 50 AD.
113: the Iazyges keep the Tisza steppe when Dacia becomes a Roman province.

c. 200: the Goths take the western Pontic steppe. 'In the 3rd century AD, the Germanic Goths broke the Sarmatian dominance of the Pontic Steppe' and the page gives 'around 200'; Cliopatria's Gothia begins in 207.
260: the Goths spread to the Donets.

wars.name: Sarmatian conquest of Scythia
wars.outcome: Sarmatian victory: the Don crossed after the Scythian defeats of 339 and 313 BC; 'By 200 BC, the Sarmatians replaced the Scythians as the dominant people of the steppes'; the Scythians reduced to Crimea, the lower Dnieper and Dobruja.

wars.name: Sarmatian wars with Rome
wars.outcome: In May 92 the Iazyges annihilated Legio XXI Rapax; they fought Rome in the Marcomannic War 'between 169 and 175' and invaded Roman Dacia in 123; no border moved on the page.

wars.name: Alan raid on Armenia and Media
wars.outcome: The Alans raided Asia Minor through the Caucasus, ravaging Media and Armenia in 135 and were driven back by Arrian, governor of Cappadocia.

wars.name: Gothic conquest of the Pontic steppe
wars.outcome: The Goths broke the Sarmatian dominance of the Pontic Steppe in the 3rd century (the page also says around 200).

wars.name: Hunnic conquest of the Alans
wars.outcome: The Huns conquered most of the Alans east of the Don in 375; many Alans migrated west.

certainty.note: Tribal confederations of mobile pastoralists: no source gives a border.
